about: MEM-3 (release C): the three new interface strings of the card memory judge, in every interface language. Read by tools/patches/mem_judge_c_i18n.py, which adds them to tools/i18n/<lang>/ui.json. Written by the main model; not read by native speakers. Each language keeps the register of its interface (du, tu, tú, ты and so on where the interface is informal). Hmong uses only words of tools/hmong/GLOSSARY.tsv and of the existing Hmong interface ("txoj kev xaiv", "qhov teb", "kuaj xyuas", "zaus", "so" for a rest); "app" stays English there as elsewhere, and "forecast" is said as "app xav" (the app thinks). The two buttons under the shown answer reuse the existing "Again" and "Got it".

keys.key: No choices this time. Say it from memory, then check.
keys.context: Review and the quizzes: the hint on a recall question. The card shows only the meaning, with no four options to pick from; the learner says the word to themselves and then taps "Show answer". Shown on a card that is one right answer away from being called memorized
Review and the quizzes: the button on a recall question that reveals the word. Short UI label

keys.key: Forecast for your last {n} answers after a break: {n}% right. Result: {n}%.
keys.context: Progress, How you learn: one line under the four bars. First number: how many of the learner's recent answers came half a day or more after the card was last seen (10 or more). Second: the share the app expected to be right. Third: the share that was right. The count is written so that it reads correctly at any number
